scope: Source-to-parameter/equation check and read-only review of bounded deterministic synthetic bolus implementation, report reconstruction and test adequacy; no review of population simulation or clinical prediction accuracy.

source_check.material: Full journal PDF pages5 and12 rendered and visually inspected; equations/rate meanings/Figure3 and Table2 independently compared with parameter JSON and code.
source_interpretations_retained: Eq3 printed ka1(t) treated as per-person constant, consistent with figure and surrounding definitions.
Mass states and dose normalized to mU/kg so division by L/kg produces mU/L.
kd=ka2+alpha; fixed effects at eta=0 and zero BMI deviation are not an arithmetic mean person.
Delayed bolus jump and zero prior history are declared synthetic choices, not recovered experimental initial conditions.

review_result.conclusion: No material discrepancy found for the declared fixed-parameter synthetic example.
code_findings: Closed form agrees algebraically with the triangular three-state ODE.
Numerical solver starts at exact tau and input jump; pending-input bookkeeping preserves dose accounting before tau.
Rates, volume, delay and concentration conversion agree with checked source and explicit normalization.
Sampled peak and trapezoidal AUC are labelled as grid-derived numerical summaries.
Distinct-rate limitation of the closed form is explicit; no arbitrary-parameter robustness or empirical-validation claim inferred.
review_result.tests_assessment: Inspected tests meaningfully cover independent matrix-exponential agreement, delayed event, complete mass accounting, zero input, fixed-parameter linear scaling, positivity, tight solvers and invalid inputs. Adequate for this bounded reference; tests were not rerun by this reviewer. Parent-reported passes are not counted as a new reviewer test execution.

import sys,json
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import quad
sys.path.insert(0,'experiments/literature/lit001/runtime')
from model import Parameters,analytic
p=Parameters.from_record(json.load(open('experiments/literature/lit001/parameters.json')))
d=200
finite_auc,err=quad(lambda t:float(analytic(np.array([t]),d,p)[0,2]/p.volume),0,600,points=[p.tau],epsabs=1e-8)
end=analytic(np.array([600.0]),d,p)[0]
expected_total=d/(p.volume*p.ke)
remaining_auc=(d-end[3])/(p.volume*p.ke)
assert abs(finite_auc+remaining_auc-expected_total)<1e-7
report=json.load(open('results/lit001/reference-02/report.json'))
print({'finite_auc':finite_auc,'total_auc':expected_total,'tail_auc':remaining_auc,'stored_auc':report['trapezoid_auc_mU_min_per_L']})
additional_executed_check.formula: Integral_0^600 y(t)dt + [SC1(600)+SC2(600)+plasma(600)]/(V_I*k_e) = dose/(V_I*k_e). All remaining insulin eventually passes the sole systemic elimination process under this fixed linear model.
additional_executed_check.independence_limit: Adaptive quadrature uses the implemented analytic concentration function; the expected complete AUC is derived independently from dose, volume and clearance. This complements solver checks, but is not a separate empirical model validation or second independent implementation.
additional_executed_check.stored_trapezoid_interpretation: Difference from adaptive quadrature is about0.00129441mU*min/L, consistent with the finite0.25min trapezoid grid; no empirical accuracy tolerance implied.
